headline: Funding flows. Satellites launch. Defense contracts grow.
deck: This week saw significant investments and launches in the space sector, with a notable focus on defense and communication technologies.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190 million in a Series C funding round, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The company focuses on co-orbital security and space domain awareness, riding the wave of increasing DoD interest in these capabilities. With this cash influx, True Anomaly is poised to expand its operational reach in a market that’s becoming more crowded by the day.
stories.soWhat: In a world where space threats are becoming more tangible, True Anomaly's funding is a reminder that cash is king, even if the innovation is just a side dish.

stories.head: Rocket Lab's 10th Synspective satellite launched
stories.body: Rocket Lab successfully launched its 10th Synspective satellite, marking a steady progression in its partnership with the Japanese startup. The launch adds to the growing constellation aimed at providing advanced Earth observation services. At approximately $5 million per launch, Rocket Lab continues to demonstrate that persistence can pay off, albeit at a premium.
stories.soWhat: Rocket Lab's consistency in launching satellites shows that in the space game, reliability can sometimes outweigh the flashiness of a single blockbuster launch.

stories.head: Anduril and L3Harris team for tactical SDA bid
stories.body: Anduril and L3Harris are collaborating on a bid for a tactical Space Development Agency (SDA) constellation, combining Anduril's defense tech prowess with L3Harris's satellite expertise. This partnership comes as the DoD pushes for more integrated space capabilities, highlighting the growing importance of collaboration in defense contracts. The exact financial terms of the bid remain undisclosed, but expect it to be competitive.
stories.soWhat: In defense, partnerships can be as fleeting as a shooting star, but this one could signal a shift toward more integrated space solutions.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on FOSSA's next moves
watchlist.body: With $10.5 million in fresh capital, FOSSA Systems could redefine satellite communications in Spain—watch for their next announcement.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN program extension
watchlist.body: Palantir's $480 million extension is a signal that government contracts are still a lucrative game, but can they keep innovating?

watchlist.title: Hypersonic glide-vehicle tests delayed again
watchlist.body: With delays piling up for the third quarter in a row, the hypersonic program might need to rethink its timeline—investors will be watching closely.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
